newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Mayor during Vukovar massacre held for war crimes.
newsitem.headline: Mayor during Vukovar massacre held for war crimes.

text.p: The U.N. war crimes tribunal said on Friday it had arrested a Serb ex-mayor of Vukovar under whose control one of the former Yugoslavia's first exercises in ethnic cleansing was carried out.

"Slavko Dokmanovic was arrested on 27 June 1997 by ICTY (International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia) investigators in Eastern Slavonia...He was then transferred to The Netherlands," the tribunal said in a statement.

It said Slavko Dokmanovic was President of Vukovar Municipality in the eastern Slavonian region of Croatia in November 1991, when the JNA (Yugoslavia People's Army) and Serb paramilitaries abducted around 260 men from the city's hospital.
"(The men) were later transported in groups to a site close to Ovcara where they were shot and killed," the statement said.
Forensic experts uncovered 200 bodies from the site, located to the southeast of Vukovar, in 1996.

The tribunal gave no details of the charges to be faced by Dokmanovic, who was indicted on March 26 last year in an unpublished amendment to the so-called "Vukovar indictment" earlier issued against three Yugoslav People's Army (JNA) officers for their involvement in the alleged massacre.

It said details of the charges against Dokmanovic had not been made public at the time in order to facilitate his arrest, and would be clarified by the tribunal's chief prosecutor Louise Arbour at a news conference on Monday.
Dokmanovic was being held at the tribunal's detention cells in Scheveningen near The Hague, the tribunal said.
His arrest brings to nine the number of war crimes suspects held in ICTY custody.

Since it was established in May 1993 as the first international body for the prosecution of war crimes since the post-World War Two Nuremberg and Tokyo trials, the tribunal has indicted 75 suspects, the majority of whom are Serbs.
Its two most prominent indicted suspects are former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic and former Bosnian Serb military commander Ratko Mladic, both of whom remain at large.
